messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] error with function backTransform
parts:
Dear Luciana,

I think that by "backtransform my models" you mean getting predictions of lambda or p, right ? That is, the values of mean abundance and detection that one would expect for chosen values of your covariates, given your model ?

In that case you must use the predict function. As always in R, you first define a new data frame that contains the values for the covariates at which you want to predict lambda or p. Then you call the predict function and supply this new data frame. Here is a template (note also how you must specify factors):

# Two new data sets for prediction: for lambda and for p (200 data points each)

lamNewData <- data.frame(elev = (seq(200, 2250,,200) - mean(tits[,"elev"]))/ sd(tits[,"elev"]), forest = 0, iLength = 1/5.1)

pNewData <- data.frame(elev = 0, time = factor("2", levels = c("1", "2", "3")), dur = 0, date = (seq(1,90,,200) - mean(date, na.rm = T))/sd(date, na.rm = T))


In the new data frames you must specify a value of all covariates that appear in the abundance or the detection part of the model. Note that in my example, I had standardised all covariates (with the exception of iLength), so that a value of 0 corresponds to the average of those covariates.

Once you have that you do something like:

# Predictions for lambda and p, with SE and CIs

predict(fm5, type="state", newdata=lamNewData)    # predictions for expected abundance (lambda)

predict(fm5, type="det", newdata=pNewData)        # same for detection probability


Kind regards  -- Marc
